newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re plans statement on ART unit.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re plans statement on ART unit.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co said it intended to release a statement later on Monday on plans to spin off its Alternative Risk Transfer (ART) actitivies as a separate legal unit.
The world's second biggest reinsurer said the statement was scheduled after the Swiss stock exchange closes at 4:30 pm (1430 GMT).
"We will release a statement on this issue after the bourse closes today," Swiss Re spokesman Andreas Jaeggi said.

Swiss Re last week confirmed a Swiss newspaper report that it planned to set up a separate unit for alternative risk transfer, a new but growing business in the financial world that combines derivative instruments with insurance and risk management.
Analysts said a legally independent ART subsidiary could be a promising sideline for Swiss Re.
"This has the potential to be a good business but we need more details first," said Beat Alpiger of Bank Baer in Zurich.
The weekly newspaper SonntagsZeitung reported last week the new unit would be named Swiss Re New Markets and would initially be 100-percent owned by Swiss Re.
SonntagsZeitung speculated that Credit Suisse Group could later take a stake in the new Swiss Re unit. Swiss Re declined to comment on this last week.
Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Re have been cooperating in alternative risk transfer since 1995 and the two companies have formed three joint ventures in this area.

Alternative risk transfer is one way world insurers are trying to answer concerns that there may not be enough capital in traditional insurance markets to cover large natural catastrophes, such as earthquakes.
One way to cover such risks is to securitise them by creating a marketable instrument, which then can be sold to a much larger group of investors.
So far the only derivatives on catastrophes are traded on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
